phases.name: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
phases.description: Keep the supplied targets distinct from design choices, then assemble a bounded online path for recommendation requests.

phases.name: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
phases.description: Publish interaction events asynchronously, transform them with Dataflow, and make online features and historical data available.

phases.name: Train, validate, and serve model versions
phases.description: Separate incremental update work from serving, validate each model version, and promote it through an explicit registry boundary.

phases.name: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
phases.description: Assign and measure product experiments, observe service and data health, then validate the stated latency, audience, event, uplift, and cost targets.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Freeze the current DynamoDB brief before designing
steps.content: This review draft is checked against the frozen local problem fixture for cloud_gcp_011; no live DynamoDB lookup was performed. Title: Design a Personalized Recommendation Engine. Description: Design a recommendation system that analyzes user behavior, trains ML models, generates personalized recommendations, and serves predictions via API. Requirements (verbatim): Generate personalized recommendations; Track user behavior; Train recommendation models; Serve real-time predictions; Handle cold-start problem; Implement A/B testing; Monitor recommendation quality; Update models incrementally. Constraints (verbatim): Recommendation latency under 100ms; Support 1M+ active users; Improve click-through rate by 20%; Process 100M+ events daily; Cost-effective model training. Hints (verbatim): Recommendations AI for pre-built models; BigQuery ML for custom models; Dataflow for feature engineering; Cloud Run for serving; Vertex AI for advanced ML; Memorystore for caching. The brief does not specify request cohorts, the latency statistic and boundaries, user/item cardinality beyond the stated active-user target, event schema, feature freshness, model family, update cadence, retention policy, or experiment assignment policy. Treat those as open design inputs; the targets are not measured results.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Put a stable API boundary in front of recommendation traffic
steps.content: Use the existing API Gateway catalog component as the public request boundary for prediction and behavior-event endpoints. The brief requires predictions through an API but does not name an API product or authentication policy; keep those choices configurable.

component.label: Recommendation API Gateway
component.description: API boundary for prediction and behavior-event requests

properties.purpose: Expose prediction and behavior-event API boundaries, validate request shape, and apply the selected identity and admission policies before Cloud Run handles work.

component.highlightReason: The brief explicitly requires real-time predictions through an API; the catalog has a matching API gateway component.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Keep request orchestration on Cloud Run
steps.content: Represent Cloud Run with the existing backend-server type. This service validates the request, selects the experiment arm, reads features, invokes the selected recommendation path, and returns the response. The catalog has no Cloud Run-specific node, so the provider product stays in the editable component label and purpose.

component.label: Cloud Run Recommendation API

properties.purpose: Validate prediction requests, obtain the assigned experiment arm and relevant online features, invoke the selected recommender, and return ranked results through the API. Keep provider calls bounded by the end-to-end latency target.

component.highlightReason: Cloud Run is a supplied serving hint and backend-server is the existing catalog role for request orchestration.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Route API requests into the serving service
steps.content: Pass prediction requests and accepted behavior events through the API boundary to Cloud Run. Keep the request identity and event correlation data consistent so outcomes can be joined to exposures without adding identity fields that the brief has not defined.

connection.label: Prediction and event API
connection.description: The gateway forwards validated requests to the Cloud Run orchestration service.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Add a cache for reusable online results
steps.content: Use the catalog cache component to represent Memorystore. Cache only results or features whose key includes the relevant user, item, context, and model or experiment version; define freshness from product behavior instead of choosing a TTL unsupported by the brief.

component.label: Memorystore Online Cache
component.description: Reusable recommendation results and hot online features

properties.purpose: Cache reusable recommendation results or hot feature lookups with keys that include the relevant request context and model version; choose freshness and invalidation behavior from product requirements.

component.highlightReason: Memorystore is an explicit hint and the existing cache component represents its role without inventing a cache duration.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Use cache-aside behavior without making cache correctness authoritative
steps.content: Cloud Run may read a reusable entry and refresh it from the selected recommender on a miss. A cache miss or eviction must still reach the correct source; do not let cached output cross users, experiment arms, or model versions.

connection.label: Context-scoped cache lookup
connection.description: Cloud Run uses Memorystore for eligible results and feature lookups while retaining a source-backed miss path.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Separate online features from event history
steps.content: Use the generic feature-store component for user and item features needed by online inference. Its backing GCP product and the required freshness are not named in the brief; keep the logical role separate from the historical warehouse and validate the product mapping before implementation.

component.label: Online User and Item Features
component.description: Serving-time feature lookup for personalization and cold start

properties.purpose: Serve the user and item signals required by the selected ranking path, with feature definitions and freshness aligned between online inference and model training. Confirm the GCP backing service and freshness contract.

component.highlightReason: The existing feature-store type captures the online model input role without claiming a specific GCP feature-store product.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Fetch online features in the request path
steps.content: Cloud Run requests only the features needed for the active serving path. Define behavior for missing, stale, or unavailable features so cold-start handling does not turn into an unbounded wait.

connection.label: User and item features
connection.description: The serving API fetches the feature values required to personalize a request.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Create a provider-neutral recommendation boundary
steps.content: Use the existing recommendation-service catalog type as the candidate and ranking boundary. The live hints name Recommendations AI for pre-built models and BigQuery ML with Vertex AI for custom models; select a path only after checking data needs, model-update behavior, evaluation evidence, and the latency target.

component.label: Candidate Generation and Ranking
component.description: Personalized candidate selection and ranking boundary

properties.purpose: Generate personalized candidates and rank them from online user and item features. Keep the provider choice replaceable between the supplied Recommendations AI pre-built option and a validated custom model path.

component.highlightReason: The catalog includes a recommendation-service component matching the central personalized recommendation capability.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Supply the recommender with aligned features
steps.content: Pass the online feature view to candidate generation and ranking. Keep feature transformations consistent with the definitions used in training, and include the selected item and user context needed for cold-start behavior.

connection.label: Online feature values
connection.description: The recommendation boundary consumes serving-time user and item features.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Return ranked results to the API service
steps.content: Return ranked item identifiers and the response metadata required by the API. Apply eligibility and availability rules before delivery; the brief does not define a response size or a result-list policy.

connection.label: Ranked candidate response
connection.description: The selected recommendation implementation returns eligible ranked candidates to Cloud Run.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Turn the under-100ms target into an observable contract
steps.content: The brief says Recommendation latency under 100ms but does not define the request cohort, start and end events, or the statistic used. Agree those boundaries and measure the complete API path, including cache behavior, feature reads, candidate generation, ranking, and response delivery. Allocate and bound dependency work from traces; do not claim the target is met from component-level timings alone.

decision.question: How should the service respond when a recommendation dependency consumes the request budget?
decision.chosen: Bound online dependency work and use a product-approved fallback path before the end-to-end target is exceeded.
decision.chosenReason: The latency target applies to the served recommendation, so an optional slow dependency must not hold the whole request indefinitely.

alternatives.option: Wait for every feature and model call
alternatives.tradeoff: May return a more complete result but allows a slow dependency to dominate request latency.

alternatives.option: Return cached output without checking its context
alternatives.tradeoff: Can be fast but may leak results across users, variants, or model versions.

properties.purpose: Validate prediction requests, obtain the assigned experiment arm and relevant online features, invoke the selected recommender, and return ranked results through the API. Bound dependency work against the agreed end-to-end latency measurement and use only a product-approved fallback.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Choose pre-built or custom ranking with evidence
steps.content: Compare the supplied Recommendations AI pre-built option with a custom BigQuery ML and Vertex AI path against feature control, incremental update support for the chosen model, quality evaluation, and the measured serving budget. Keep the recommendation-service boundary provider-neutral so a selection can change without changing API contracts. The hint list alone does not prove either option meets the brief.

decision.question: Which model route should own candidate ranking?
decision.chosen: Keep a replaceable recommendation boundary and select a route only after a representative offline and online evaluation confirms its fit.
decision.chosenReason: The brief asks for training and incremental updates but supplies no model family, data contract, or evaluation results that would justify a provider-specific commitment.

alternatives.option: Use Recommendations AI as the only model path
alternatives.tradeoff: Uses the supplied pre-built-model hint but must be checked for the required feature and update controls.

alternatives.option: Use a custom BigQuery ML model served through Vertex AI
alternatives.tradeoff: Offers a custom path but requires validated training, rollout, and latency behavior.

properties.purpose: Generate personalized candidates and rank them from online user and item features. Keep the provider choice replaceable between Recommendations AI and a custom BigQuery ML or Vertex AI model path; select only after update behavior, evaluation, and latency fit are demonstrated.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Keep canonical item metadata available
steps.content: Represent the source of item identity, descriptive metadata, and eligibility with the existing database component. The live brief does not specify a source system, database type, or item schema; this is a logical boundary to map to the actual product catalog.

component.label: Canonical Item Catalog
component.description: Item identity, metadata, and eligibility source

properties.purpose: Provide authoritative item identifiers, descriptive attributes, and eligibility information for candidate generation and cold-start features. Map this logical boundary to the existing product catalog and its access patterns.

component.highlightReason: An existing database type can represent the item source without introducing an unsupported catalog component type.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Apply current item eligibility before serving
steps.content: Cloud Run obtains canonical item metadata or eligibility through the existing catalog boundary, then ensures candidates are valid for the requesting context. Keep this source distinct from derived user/item features.

connection.label: Item metadata and eligibility
connection.description: The API uses canonical catalog state to validate candidate items before returning them.

steps.phase: Freeze the live brief and shape the request path
steps.title: Make the cold-start path explicit
steps.content: The brief explicitly calls out cold start but does not define which users or items count as new, what context may be used, or the acceptable fallback. Use available item metadata and request context where valid, and have the product owner choose a safe fallback when personalized history is absent. Do not present a generic popularity list as an agreed requirement.

decision.question: What should be ranked when user or item interaction history is missing?
decision.chosen: Use eligible metadata and available context, with a product-approved non-personalized fallback when those signals are insufficient.
decision.chosenReason: This addresses the stated cold-start problem while leaving the fallback policy and permitted signals explicit for product review.

alternatives.option: Return no recommendation until history exists
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids weak personalization but leaves new users and items without a result.
Provides a result but may ignore context, eligibility, or the product's intended cold-start experience.

properties.purpose: Generate personalized candidates from available user and item signals. For cold start, use eligible metadata and request context where permitted, then follow the product-approved fallback when history or required features are absent.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Buffer behavior events outside the response path
steps.content: Use the existing Pub/Sub component for accepted behavior, recommendation exposure, and outcome events. Keep event publication asynchronous to prediction responses and define consent, identifiers, retention, and deletion with the product's actual policy.

component.label: Behavior and Exposure Events
component.description: Asynchronous stream of recommendation interactions and outcomes

properties.purpose: Buffer interaction, recommendation-exposure, and outcome event references for independent processing. Use idempotent consumers and a governed event contract; do not make analytics persistence a synchronous dependency of the prediction response.

component.highlightReason: Pub/Sub is an existing catalog component and matches the supplied Dataflow event-processing hint.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Publish behavior without delaying predictions
steps.content: After the request path has a result, publish the permitted event and exposure data for downstream feature and experiment analysis. Define retry and duplicate handling from the event contract; the brief supplies no event schema or retention duration.

connection.label: Interaction and exposure events
connection.description: Cloud Run emits governed event references for asynchronous processing after serving work.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Transform events with Dataflow
steps.content: Represent Dataflow with the existing stream-processor type. Transform event records into validated feature updates and historical facts, preserving event provenance and replay safety; agree event-time and late-arrival semantics before implementation.

component.label: Dataflow Feature Pipeline
component.description: Validated event processing for online features and history

properties.purpose: Validate and transform behavior and exposure events into feature updates and historical records. Preserve event identity and replay safety, and define late-event handling from the actual event contract.

component.highlightReason: Dataflow is an explicit feature-engineering hint and stream-processor is the catalog's matching processing role.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Process the event stream independently
steps.content: Dataflow consumes the behavior and exposure stream, applies the agreed schema and deduplication rules, and publishes derived outputs. Event processing capacity and freshness remain measurements to establish against the stated daily event target.

connection.label: Behavior event stream
connection.description: Dataflow processes the asynchronous event stream for feature and historical-data consumers.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Retain analytical history for model work
steps.content: Use the existing data-warehouse type to represent BigQuery history for model training and quality analysis. The brief gives an event-volume target but does not define retention, partitioning, or data residency; decide those from workload and policy evidence.

component.label: BigQuery Interaction History
component.description: Historical behavior and exposure data for training and evaluation

properties.purpose: Store governed historical interactions, recommendation exposures, and outcomes for BigQuery ML training and quality analysis. Set retention and physical layout only after query, policy, and cost needs are known.

component.highlightReason: BigQuery ML is a supplied custom-model hint and the existing data-warehouse component represents its historical data boundary.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Persist validated history for training and analysis
steps.content: Write validated interaction and exposure records to BigQuery for custom model training and offline evaluation. Keep raw or replayable source references according to the agreed policy rather than assuming indefinite event retention.

connection.label: Validated events and outcomes
connection.description: Dataflow writes governed historical records used by training and recommendation-quality analysis.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Update online features from validated events
steps.content: Publish derived user and item feature updates to the online feature boundary. Keep the transformation definition shared with training and expose feature age so the serving path can handle missing or stale values deliberately.

connection.label: Derived feature updates
connection.description: Validated event processing refreshes serving-time user and item features.

steps.phase: Capture behavior and maintain usable features
steps.title: Define event quality and feature freshness before scaling
steps.content: Agree which user actions count as behavior, how recommendation exposures and outcomes are joined, how duplicates and late events are handled, and what feature freshness the serving model needs. The current brief does not define these contracts; record them before interpreting daily volume or model quality.

decision.question: How should incomplete or repeated behavior events affect feature updates?
decision.chosen: Validate an explicit event contract, deduplicate by its stable event identity, and make late or invalid records visible for replay or correction.
decision.chosenReason: Training and online personalization depend on trustworthy event-derived features, while the brief does not define event identity or late-arrival semantics.

alternatives.tradeoff: Simple but can double-count retries or admit malformed signals into features.

alternatives.option: Drop records that arrive outside an arbitrary window
alternatives.tradeoff: Can silently bias training and feature state without a business-approved lateness policy.

properties.purpose: Validate and transform behavior and exposure events under an agreed event contract. Deduplicate by its stable event identity, preserve replayability, and make late or invalid records visible for correction.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Separate model-update work from user requests
steps.content: Use the existing queue component for model-update work requests. This separates training and validation from interactive serving and makes failed updates retryable without tying a model job to a prediction request.

component.label: Model Update Work Queue
component.description: Asynchronous requests to train and validate model versions

properties.purpose: Buffer model-update requests independently of online prediction traffic so training, validation, retries, and promotion do not block recommendation responses.

component.highlightReason: The existing queue type represents asynchronous model-update work without adding a new component type.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Trigger update evaluation from new data
steps.content: Dataflow or a governed warehouse workflow can enqueue an update request when new feature and history state is ready. Define the trigger condition and cadence from the model's supported update method and observed data, not from a guessed event threshold.

connection.label: New training data available
connection.description: Validated feature and event progress can request an asynchronous model update evaluation.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Train custom models from governed history
steps.content: Represent the training workflow with the existing model-training type and the supplied BigQuery ML hint. Keep algorithm, labels, evaluation cohort, and supported incremental-update mechanism open until the data and product contracts are defined.

component.label: BigQuery ML Model Training
component.description: Training and validation workflow for recommendation model versions

properties.purpose: Train and evaluate custom recommendation models from governed BigQuery history and aligned feature definitions. Confirm that the selected model family supports the required incremental update behavior before claiming this requirement is met.

component.highlightReason: Model training is an explicit requirement and the catalog has a dedicated model-training component.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Run model updates outside the serving path
steps.content: The training workflow consumes queued update requests, reads an agreed snapshot or incrementally updated training view, and produces a candidate model version. Preserve the data and feature lineage used to create each candidate.

connection.label: Model update request
connection.description: Queued work starts an isolated training and validation run.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Make incremental updates a tested model capability
steps.content: The brief requires incremental model updates but does not define the algorithm, update unit, cadence, or quality guardrails. Select a model and update workflow that demonstrably incorporates new data without silently discarding the current good version; if the selected BigQuery ML or Vertex AI approach cannot meet that contract, surface the gap rather than relabeling full retraining as incremental.

decision.question: What should happen when a candidate incremental update fails quality validation?
decision.chosen: Keep the current serving version active, retain the rejected candidate and its evaluation evidence, and retry only after the cause is addressed.
decision.chosenReason: An update should not degrade recommendations merely because new data arrived; incremental behavior and quality must be demonstrated together.

alternatives.tradeoff: Ensures new data is incorporated but can replace a better model with a degraded one.
May be easier to operate but does not by itself satisfy the stated incremental-update requirement.

properties.purpose: Train and evaluate custom recommendation models from governed history and aligned features. Use a model-supported incremental update workflow, preserve the current good version on failed validation, and retain lineage and evaluation evidence for every candidate.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Track validated model versions
steps.content: Use the existing model-registry component to retain candidate identity, training inputs, feature definitions, evaluation results, and promotion state. A model artifact is not ready for serving merely because training completed.

component.label: Recommendation Model Registry
component.description: Version and promotion record for trained models

properties.purpose: Version model artifacts with their training data, feature definitions, evaluation evidence, and explicit candidate, accepted, or rejected state before deployment.

component.highlightReason: The catalog includes a model registry suited to explicit version and promotion tracking.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Register candidates with their evaluation evidence
steps.content: Publish a candidate only after its agreed offline checks complete. Record which event and feature definitions produced it so later quality changes can be traced to a model version and its inputs.

connection.label: Candidate model and evaluation
connection.description: Training registers a version together with its lineage and validation evidence.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Serve a promoted custom model through Vertex AI
steps.content: Represent the custom online model endpoint with the existing model-serving type and the supplied Vertex AI hint. Keep model-specific deployment configuration and serving capacity tied to measured demand and the agreed latency contract.

component.label: Vertex AI Recommendation Model
component.description: Online inference for a promoted custom model

properties.purpose: Serve only a promoted custom recommendation model version for online inference. Confirm model-specific deployment, feature compatibility, and measured serving behavior against the API latency target.

component.highlightReason: The supplied Vertex AI hint maps to the existing model-serving component.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Promote only an accepted registry version
steps.content: Deploy a registry version only after the agreed validation and release checks. Retain a clear way to restore the previously accepted version if live quality or serving behavior regresses.

connection.label: Accepted model version
connection.description: The serving endpoint receives a version that passed the defined promotion checks.

steps.phase: Train, validate, and serve model versions
steps.title: Separate model quality from model availability
steps.content: Define offline relevance checks and online guardrails for each model version, including the CTR experiment goal and any user-experience measures the product selects. No achieved lift or quality threshold beyond the brief's target is supplied. Keep the existing model serving until the candidate has evidence appropriate to its rollout.

decision.question: When is a trained recommendation model eligible for promotion?
decision.chosen: Promote only after reproducible offline evaluation, feature compatibility checks, and a controlled online plan with observable rollback signals.
decision.chosenReason: Training completion alone does not show that recommendations are useful or that the model can serve within the requested latency.

alternatives.option: Promote as soon as training finishes
alternatives.tradeoff: Reduces release delay but skips evidence that quality and serving contracts still hold.

alternatives.option: Require the brief's CTR target before any exposure
alternatives.tradeoff: Can prevent learning from a controlled experiment because the target itself is an outcome to measure.

properties.purpose: Serve only a promoted custom recommendation model version with feature compatibility and reproducible evaluation evidence. Retain a rollback path and verify live quality and latency during controlled rollout.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Represent product experiment assignment explicitly
steps.content: The catalog's experiment-tracking component is for model-run comparisons and does not represent assigning product users to recommendation variants or recording their exposure. Use its existing generic custom component for this genuine catalog gap; keep the assignment key and allocation policy open until the product defines them.

component.label: Product A/B Assignment and Exposure
component.description: Product-level variant assignment and exposure record

properties.subtitle: Product experiment control
properties.purpose: Assign the product-defined recommendation variant and record eligible exposure for outcome analysis. The assignment key, allocation, enrollment, and exclusion rules remain to be defined with the product team.
properties.componentType: Catalog gap: product A/B assignment and exposure service
properties.technology: Existing product experimentation platform, if available
properties.notes: No dedicated user-to-variant assignment component exists in the catalog. The model experiment-tracking component does not provide this product assignment role.

component.highlightReason: The existing catalog lacks product experiment assignment and exposure semantics; this is the sole generic custom component in the draft.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Assign an experiment arm before recommendation selection
steps.content: Cloud Run requests the product-defined assignment using the agreed subject and experiment context. Ensure retries preserve the same assignment semantics; do not assume a user identifier or allocation policy that the brief has not provided.

connection.label: Variant assignment request
connection.description: The request service obtains the experiment arm under the product-defined assignment policy.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Apply the assigned variant consistently
steps.content: Return the selected arm to Cloud Run so it can route to the corresponding recommendation configuration. Keep control and treatment behavior explicit in the experiment plan and avoid mixing variants through shared cache keys.

connection.label: Assigned recommendation variant
connection.description: Cloud Run applies the returned arm when choosing recommendation behavior and cache context.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Pass the selected variant into recommendation logic
steps.content: Cloud Run passes the assigned model or ranking configuration to the recommendation boundary. The variant choice should not change user eligibility rules or the event definitions used to compare outcomes.

connection.label: Context and assigned variant
connection.description: Cloud Run invokes the recommendation boundary with the selected experiment configuration.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Call the custom model only for the selected route
steps.content: When the chosen route uses the custom model, the recommendation boundary requests inference from Vertex AI with the compatible feature view. The pre-built Recommendations AI option remains an alternative at this same semantic boundary, not an extra serial call on every request.

connection.label: Selected custom model request
connection.description: The recommendation boundary calls Vertex AI only when the selected implementation is the custom model route.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Return model scores to candidate ranking
steps.content: Return scores or ranking signals to the recommendation boundary for eligibility filtering and final response assembly. Define the score meaning and tie-breaking behavior with the selected model; the brief gives no ranking formula.

connection.label: Model scores and ranking signals
connection.description: Custom model output returns to the recommendation boundary for final candidate handling.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Measure recommendation quality from governed outcomes
steps.content: Use the existing analytics component for offline and online recommendation-quality views. Include the agreed exposure and outcome definitions, segment results only by legitimate product cohorts, and keep the CTR goal separate from measured performance.

component.label: Recommendation Quality Analytics

properties.purpose: Analyze governed recommendation exposures, user outcomes, and model quality with agreed definitions. Distinguish the stated click-through-rate goal from observed experiment results.

component.highlightReason: The existing analytics component matches recommendation-quality and outcome analysis.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Record exposures and user outcomes for analysis
steps.content: Emit the experiment arm, eligible exposure, returned recommendation context, and agreed downstream outcome references. Avoid attributing an outcome to a recommendation without the experiment's defined join and attribution policy.

connection.label: Exposure and request context
connection.description: The serving path emits governed exposure references for quality and experiment analysis.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Join outcomes to historical interaction data
steps.content: Use the governed BigQuery history to calculate agreed offline quality and experiment outcomes. Preserve the event and model-version lineage used for each result so comparisons remain interpretable after model updates.

connection.label: Historical outcomes and exposures
connection.description: Analytics joins governed history with model and experiment versions for offline evaluation.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Observe serving health separately from model quality
steps.content: Use the existing monitoring component for request latency, errors, dependency health, cache behavior, and capacity signals. Keep operational health distinct from offline relevance and experiment outcome analytics.

component.label: Recommendation Service Monitoring
component.description: Operational health of the online and event-processing paths

properties.purpose: Observe API latency and errors, model and feature dependencies, cache behavior, event-processing health, and measured capacity. Do not treat infrastructure health as proof of recommendation quality.

component.highlightReason: The existing monitoring component covers operational metrics without conflating them with product-quality analytics.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Trace the full online prediction path
steps.content: Instrument the gateway-to-response path and its cache, feature, recommender, and model dependencies. Use the agreed latency boundary and cohort labels while excluding sensitive event payloads from operational logs.

connection.label: Request latency and dependency health
connection.description: The online service exports operational signals for the complete prediction path.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Observe event lag and data quality
steps.content: Export event backlog age, processing failures, duplicate and late-event counts, and feature freshness. Define operational thresholds only after the pipeline is measured against the event-volume and product freshness needs.

connection.label: Event lag and feature freshness
connection.description: Dataflow reports processing health and freshness signals for operational response.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Treat the 20% click-through goal as an experiment outcome
steps.content: The brief asks to improve click-through rate by 20% but gives no baseline, denominator, attribution window, eligible population, or guardrails. Predefine those with the product team and compare a controlled experiment with a valid baseline. Do not claim the target is achieved from recommendation clicks alone if exposure, downstream outcomes, or user experience are not accounted for.

decision.question: What evidence would support the stated click-through improvement goal?
decision.chosen: Use a product-approved controlled experiment with consistent exposure logging, a declared baseline and denominator, and reviewable outcome and user-experience guardrails.
decision.chosenReason: The brief states a goal, not an observed result or measurement method; controlled attribution makes the result auditable.

alternatives.option: Compare raw clicks before and after launch
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy to calculate but confounded by traffic, placement, seasonality, and user mix.
Useful during training but does not establish the requested online click-through improvement.

properties.purpose: Analyze governed recommendation exposures, user outcomes, and model quality with predeclared experiment definitions. Evaluate the stated 20% click-through improvement goal against an agreed baseline, denominator, attribution, and user-experience guardrails; report results as measured evidence.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Validate the active-user and request-latency targets
steps.content: Load-test a representative workload that supports the stated 1M+ active-user target while measuring the agreed end-to-end recommendation latency. The brief does not specify concurrent-user behavior, request rate, cohort mix, or geographic distribution, so capacity must be derived from workload evidence rather than from an invented traffic multiplier.

scaleTrigger.metric: Active users, observed request arrival and concurrency, end-to-end recommendation latency, cache hit behavior, feature-store latency, and model endpoint saturation
scaleTrigger.action: Scale the Cloud Run and model-serving capacity from measured workload and dependency saturation, and retest the complete API path against the agreed under-100ms contract.
scaleTrigger.impact: Tests whether the serving design supports 1M+ active users and Recommendation latency under 100ms; neither target is claimed as achieved.

properties.purpose: Validate prediction requests, obtain the assigned experiment arm and relevant online features, invoke the selected recommender, and return ranked results through the API. Scale from measured active-user workload and dependency saturation; verify the agreed end-to-end latency contract.

steps.phase: Experiment, observe, and define acceptance evidence
steps.title: Validate daily event processing and training cost together
steps.content: Exercise the stated 100M+ daily event target with realistic event shape and processing behavior. Observe backlog, feature freshness, training work, and spend; choose worker and update capacity from measured throughput and the approved research budget. The brief does not specify a freshness deadline or cost ceiling.

scaleTrigger.metric: Daily event volume, oldest-event age, processing throughput, feature freshness, queued model-update work, and measured training and storage cost
